answer: A reputation that moves like a glacier defeats cheap copies: a new identity starts with zero weight and earns influence only slowly, as unrelated peers verify its useful work over weeks. Endorsements are capped and decay unless the agent keeps contributing, so a fake cannot buy standing overnight. Like a sonnet, the record must scan: praise from one clique counts little, while broad, sustained approval counts more. Facing this horizon, an attacker must do real work for every clone, month after month, turning forgery from a free flood into a labor bill that grows with each fake.
